paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: tragedy is not a report card. Some people told Jesus about Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices, and then Jesus brought up eighteen people killed when the tower of Siloam collapsed. Both times He asked whether they were worse sinners than everybody else, and both times He said, "No, I tell you." (Luke 13:2-5) So when something terrible happens to somebody, we don't get to say they had it coming.

But then Jesus turns the question around, and it lands on the one asking. Twice He says, "But unless you repent, you too will all perish." (Luke 13:3, 5) Friend, I came to Jesus in the first place with my hands full of dust, so I'm not going to wave a finger at anybody. Instead of grading everybody else's mess, we're told to look at our own hearts and turn back to God.

And look at the fig tree. After three years with no fruit, the owner says, "Cut it down!" but the keeper of the vineyard says, "leave it alone again this year." (Luke 13:7-8) That extra year is room to turn around, and I know a thing or two about being given room. It's not a promise that the wait lasts forever, though, so today is a good day to bear fruit. This teaching isn't over, friend, so stay tuned.
